title: Missing input validation for config properties

evidence.quote:
const whatWeKnow = config.whatWeKnow
  const intakeSaved = Boolean(intake)

{typeof whatWeKnow === 'string' ? (
{whatWeKnow}
) : (

reasoning: In Welcome.tsx:420-432, code assumes whatWeKnow is either a string or an array-like object with .map() method, but doesn't validate it's truthy or handle null/undefined. If whatWeKnow is null/undefined/number/boolean, the ternary will fall through to the else branch and call .map() on a non-array, causing a runtime crash. Similarly, About.tsx checks length but doesn't validate the array items have required icon/title/body properties before rendering at line 173-176.
reproduction: Set config.whatWeKnow to null, undefined, or a non-string/non-array value. The component will attempt to call .map() on the value and throw 'whatWeKnow.map is not a function'.
recommendation: Add runtime validation: in Welcome.tsx, check `Array.isArray(whatWeKnow)` before the ternary's else branch. In About.tsx, validate each point object has required fields (icon, title, body) before rendering, or provide defaults.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included in this feature to validate config shape or runtime rendering behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test that renders WelcomeSection with config.whatWeKnow set to null, undefined, {}, and [] to ensure graceful handling. Similar test for AboutSection with malformed aboutPoints array items.
minimumFixScope: Add type guards in Welcome.tsx:420 and About.tsx:162 before rendering derived config data.
